questions.question: Class 1, Class 2.1, and Class 3 items should not be placed in a trailer with:
questions.explanation: Cargo heaters are not allowed when transporting Class 1 (Explosives), Class 2.1 (Flammable Gas), or Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) materials.

questions.question: If transporting explosives, you may leave your vehicle unattended:
questions.explanation: When carrying hazardous materials, you can only leave your vehicle unattended in an approved location called a safe haven.

questions.question: Flammable gases are categorized as ____ hazards.
questions.explanation: Flammable gases are classified as Class 2 hazardous materials.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a shipping paper?
questions.explanation: Shipping papers describe the hazardous materials being transported. Shipping orders, bills of lading, and manifests are all shipping papers. Directions are not.

questions.question: When refueling a vehicle that contains hazardous materials:

options.text: The engine should be left on.
The engine should be turned off.
The gas nozzle may be left unattended.
No other vehicles should be at the refueling station.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine should be turned off.
questions.explanation: Always turn off the engine before refueling a vehicle carrying hazardous materials. Someone must always be at the nozzle controlling the fuel flow.

questions.question: Materials that are considered hazardous may include all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials are products that pose risks during transportation. These include explosives, flammable gases, poisonous gases, and hazardous solids. Ordinary rocks are not hazardous materials.

questions.question: Besides reading the manual, the best way to learn about transporting hazardous materials is to:
questions.explanation: The manual contains information for the written exam, but hazardous materials training courses teach you how to safely transport these materials on the job.

questions.question: If a package contains liquid containers, the package must display:

options.text: Arrows pointing in the correct upright direction.
The number of containers inside the box.

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrows pointing in the correct upright direction.
questions.explanation: Packages with liquid containers must have arrows showing which way is up. The package must be placed in the correct upright direction during transport.

questions.question: If required, ____ identical placards must be placed on a vehicle.
questions.explanation: When hazardous materials placards are required, place four identical placards on the vehicle: one on the front, one on the back, and one on each side.

questions.question: Which type of material may be required to have a transport index?
questions.explanation: Some radioactive materials must have a transport index. This number shows how much control the material needs during transport. The total transport index in one vehicle cannot exceed 50.

questions.question: Do not smoke within ____ of a vehicle carrying Class 3 or Division 2.1 hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Do not smoke within 25 feet of a vehicle carrying Class 3 or Division 2.1 hazardous materials.

questions.question: Which statement is true about the person supervising tank loading?

options.text: Does not need to know the materials being loaded.
Must be within 25 feet of the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be within 25 feet of the tank.
questions.explanation: The supervisor must be alert, have a clear view of the tank, stay within 25 feet, know the hazards, know emergency procedures, and be able to move the tank if needed.

questions.question: Which agency conducts the background check for a HazMat endorsement?
questions.explanation: The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) conducts background checks for hazardous materials endorsements.

questions.question: Hazardous materials containers must be:

options.text: Braced to prevent movement during transportation.
A maximum of four feet tall.

questions.correctAnswerText: Braced to prevent movement during transportation.
questions.explanation: Containers must be braced so they do not fall, slide, or bounce around during transport.

questions.question: Where can you find identification numbers for hazardous chemicals?

options.text: In the DOT Emergency Response Guidebook.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the DOT Emergency Response Guidebook.
questions.explanation: The DOT Emergency Response Guidebook (ERG) lists all hazardous chemicals and their identification numbers.

questions.question: What information is in Column 2 of the Hazardous Materials Table?
questions.explanation: Column 2 lists the proper shipping names and descriptions of regulated materials.

questions.question: When loading a tank with flammable liquids, what should you do first?

options.text: Establish a ground before opening the filling hole.
Establish a ground right before opening the filling hole.
Lock the filling hole during loading.

questions.correctAnswerText: Establish a ground before opening the filling hole.
questions.explanation: Before loading flammable liquids, turn off the engine (unless needed for pumping). Ground the tank before opening the filling hole and keep it grounded until after closing the filling hole.

questions.question: Who must install placards on a vehicle?
questions.explanation: The shipper provides the placards, but the driver is responsible for placing them on the vehicle.

questions.question: Which is NOT required of the person loading a tank with hazardous materials?

options.text: Aware of the hazards associated with the materials.

questions.explanation: The supervisor must be alert, have a clear view, stay within 25 feet (not 10), know the hazards, know emergency procedures, and be able to move the tank.

questions.question: Hazardous materials regulations are meant to protect:
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials transport is risky. Regulations protect you, those around you, and the environment.

questions.question: How must placards be placed?

options.text: In any way, as long as they are visible.
So words and numbers read from left to right.
Within three inches of other markings.

questions.correctAnswerText: So words and numbers read from left to right.
questions.explanation: Placards for hazardous materials must show words and numbers that read from left to right. They must be at least three inches away from any other markings.

questions.question: What is required when transporting explosives?

options.text: You must have a written route plan.
You should take the shortest route.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must have a written route plan.
questions.explanation: When transporting explosives, you must have a written route plan and follow it. Avoid heavily populated areas, crowds, tunnels, narrow streets, and alleys when possible.

questions.question: How must a shipper tell a driver about cargo risks?

options.text: By writing a note on plain paper.
By putting hazard warning labels on packages.
By placing orange dots on packages.

questions.correctAnswerText: By putting hazard warning labels on packages.
questions.explanation: Shippers must warn drivers about hazards using shipping papers, hazard warning labels on packages, emergency response information, and placards.

questions.question: What should you do if hazardous materials leak while driving?

options.text: Park the vehicle as soon as possible.
Leave the area to find help.
Drive around looking for someone to repair the leak.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park the vehicle as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: If cargo leaks while driving, stop the vehicle right away. Continuing to drive spreads the contamination. Park safely, secure the area, and send someone else to get help.

questions.question: What should not be in a trailer with Class 1, Class 2.1, or Class 3 materials?
questions.explanation: Heaters cannot be used when transporting Class 1 (Explosives), Class 2.1 (Flammable Gas), or Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) materials.

questions.question: What is the correct way to check tire pressure?

options.text: Push on the tires to feel pressure.

questions.explanation: Check each tire at the start of every trip. A tire pressure gauge is the only way to correctly check tire pressure.

questions.question: What should you know about restrictions on transporting explosives or hazardous waste?

options.text: They are usually not a concern.
They do not apply on weekends.
Research them before choosing your route.
They only apply to loads over 1,000 pounds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Research them before choosing your route.
questions.explanation: Before transporting hazardous materials, check for any restrictions that apply to the routes you plan to take.

questions.question: What is important to know about transporting radioactive materials?

options.text: Radiation passes through to other packages.
The package should be placed in the cab.
The package should be loaded on its side.
The package should be made of wood.

questions.correctAnswerText: Radiation passes through to other packages.
questions.explanation: Radiation spreads from each radioactive package to nearby packages. Rules limit how many radioactive packages can be loaded together.

questions.question: What placard is needed if "Inhalation Hazard" is on the shipping paper?

options.text: Poison Gas or Poison Inhalation Hazard

questions.correctAnswerText: Poison Gas or Poison Inhalation Hazard
questions.explanation: If "Inhalation Hazard" appears on the shipping paper or package, display the "Poison Inhalation Hazard" or "Poison Gas" placard.

questions.question: Who must provide emergency response information?
questions.explanation: The shipper of hazardous materials must give emergency response information to drivers.
